label: Institution
name: Temple of Great Compassion
summary:
The Temple of Great Compassion (Dabei Si, 大悲寺) — one of several Chinese Buddhist temples bearing this name dedicated to Guanyin (the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion) — refers most commonly to the Dabei Si in Shenyang (capital of Liaoning Province), founded in 1640 during the late Ming/early Qing transition and one of the most important Buddhist monasteries in northeastern China. The temple name 'Great Compassion' (Dabei) directly references Guanyin's primary epithet — 'He/She Who Perceives the Sounds of the World's Suffering' and responds with infinite compassion.

The Shenyang Dabei Si was founded in 1640 (the final year of the Ming Dynasty, one year before the Qing Dynasty conquest of Beijing), making it a significant institution of the transitional Ming-Qing period in Manchuria — the homeland of the Qing's Manchu founders. The temple contains a famous Tang Dynasty (618-907 CE) Buddha statue and other important Buddhist artworks, and has been an active monastic community continuously for nearly four centuries.

Dabei Si Shenyang is notable in modern Chinese religious history as one of the few Chinese Buddhist monasteries that maintained strict traditional monastic discipline through the late 20th century under abbot Miaoxiang (1990s-2000s), attracting practitioners from across China. The temple's strict standards of practice and training have given it an unusual modern reputation as a center of rigorous Buddhist discipline. Guanyin, the bodhisattva of compassion to whom these temples are dedicated, is the most widely worshipped deity in Chinese Buddhism and one of the most beloved religious figures in all of East Asian culture.
